questions.stem: The ferry at Double Bay is being pulled into the wharf by a rope at a speed of 25m/min. The rope is attached to a point on the ferry 6m vertically below the level of the wharf. At what rate is the rope being drawn in, when the ferry is 28m from the wharf?
questions.hint: Right triangle r² = x² + 6²; dr/dt = (dr/dx)(dx/dt) with dx/dt = 25.

steps.explain: Let \(x\) be the horizontal distance to the wharf and \(r\) the rope length. They form a right triangle with the 6 m vertical side.

steps.explain: The rope comes in slightly slower than the ferry moves, because part of the motion is 'sideways' to the rope.

keyPoints.text: 6m vertically below the level of the wharf
keyPoints.note: The rope, the 6 m drop and the horizontal distance form a right triangle: r² = x² + 36.

questions.stem: A plane flies horizontally at an altitude of 10 km. It passes directly over a tracking telescope on the ground. When the angle of elevation from the telescope to the plane is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians, the angle of elevation is decreasing at a rate of \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) rad/min . How fast is the plane travelling at the time of measurement?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 210" width="300" height="210"><rect width="300" height="210" rx="8" fill="white"/><line x1="80.0" y1="180.0" x2="230.0" y2="40.0" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><line x1="230.0" y1="40.0" x2="230.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><line x1="80.0" y1="180.0" x2="230.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><path d="M220 180L220 170L230 170" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M204 36L256 36L260 40L256 43L204 43Z" fill="#1e293b"/><path d="M226 38L214 24L222 24L236 38Z" fill="#1e293b"/><text x="106.0" y="172.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="15.7" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">θ</text><text x="238.0" y="110.0" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#1e293b" text-anchor="start">10 km</text><text x="140.8" y="200.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="14.6" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">x</text><text x="148.5" y="200.0" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" font-size="13.0" fill="#1e293b"> km</text><circle cx="80.0" cy="180.0" r="4" fill="#1e293b"/></svg>

questions.hint: x = 10 cot θ; dx/dt = (dx/dθ)(dθ/dt) with dθ/dt = −π/6.

steps.explain: Let \(x\) be the horizontal distance and \(\theta\) the angle of elevation. In the right triangle the opposite side is 10.

keyPoints.text: How fast is the plane travelling
keyPoints.note: Relate x and θ with tan θ = 10/x, then use the chain rule.

questions.stem: An open flat topped water trough in the shape of a triangular prism is being emptied through a hole in its base at a constant rate of 18000 cm³ per second. Its top measures 1.5 metres by 4 metres and its triangular end has a vertical height of 25 centimetres. When the water depth is \(h\) centimetres the water surface measures \(x\) centimetres by 4 metres.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 225" width="300" height="225"><rect width="300" height="225" rx="8" fill="white"/><path d="M50.0 40.0L250.0 40.0L150.0 180.0Z" fill="#f1f5f9" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" fill-opacity="1"/><path d="M70.0 68.0L230.0 68.0L150.0 180.0Z" fill="#93c5fd" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linejoin="round" fill-opacity="0.6"/><text x="150.0" y="32.0" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#1e293b" text-anchor="middle">150 cm</text><line x1="270.0" y1="40.0" x2="270.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="276.0" y="115.0" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#1e293b" text-anchor="start">25</text><line x1="30.0" y1="68.0" x2="30.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="15.6" y="128.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="14.6" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">h</text><text x="146.2" y="62.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="14.6" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">x</text></svg>

parts.stem: Show that when the water depth is \(h\) centimetres, the volume \(V\) cm³ of water in the trough is given by \(V=1200h^2\)
parts.hint: Similar triangles give x = 6h; then V = ½xh × 400.

steps.explain: Work in cm: top width 150 cm, height 25 cm, length 400 cm. The water's triangle is similar to the end triangle.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 225" width="300" height="225"><rect width="300" height="225" rx="8" fill="white"/><path d="M50.0 40.0L250.0 40.0L150.0 180.0Z" fill="#f1f5f9" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" fill-opacity="1"/><path d="M70.0 68.0L230.0 68.0L150.0 180.0Z" fill="#93c5fd" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linejoin="round" fill-opacity="0.6"/><text x="150.0" y="32.0" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#ea580c" text-anchor="middle">150 cm</text><line x1="270.0" y1="40.0" x2="270.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#ea580c" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="276.0" y="115.0" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#ea580c" text-anchor="start">25</text><line x1="30.0" y1="68.0" x2="30.0" y2="180.0" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="15.6" y="128.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="14.6" fill="#2563eb" font-style="italic">h</text><text x="146.2" y="62.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="14.6" fill="#2563eb" font-style="italic">x</text><text x="152.8" y="190.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="9.7" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">x</text><text x="148.4" y="200.6" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" font-size="8.6" fill="#1e293b">150</text><line x1="147.4" y1="192.4" x2="163.6" y2="192.4" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.00"/><text x="165.6" y="196.0" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" font-size="12.0" fill="#1e293b"> = </text><text x="182.8" y="190.0" font-family="Times New Roman,Times,serif" font-size="9.7" fill="#1e293b" font-style="italic">h</text><text x="181.1" y="200.6" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" font-size="8.6" fill="#1e293b">25</text><line x1="180.1" y1="192.4" x2="191.6" y2="192.4" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.00"/></svg>

steps.explain: Volume of a prism = area of the end × length.

parts.answer: Similar triangles: \(\frac{x}{150}=\frac{h}{25}\Rightarrow x=6h\). V = (area of triangular end) × length = ½ · x · h · 400 = ½ · 6h · h · 400 = 1200h².

keyPoints.note: Convert metres to cm and use similar triangles: x/150 = h/25.

questions.stem: A spherical balloon is being inflated at a constant rate of \(200\pi\) cm³ s⁻¹. At what rate is the radius of the balloon increasing when the radius is 10 cm?

steps.explain: Volume of a sphere, and its derivative with respect to \(r\).
Chain rule connects the two rates.

keyPoints.text: At what rate is the radius
keyPoints.note: Use V = (4/3)πr³ and the chain rule dV/dt = (dV/dr)(dr/dt).

questions.stem: A body of still water has suffered an oil spill and a circular oil slick is floating on the surface of the water. The area of the oil slick is increasing by \(0.1\,\text{m}^2/\text{minute}\). At what rate is the radius increasing when the area is \(0.3\,\text{m}^2\)?
questions.hint: Differentiate A=πr² with respect to time, then use A=0.3 to find r at that instant.

keyPoints.note: Use the circle area relationship \(A=\pi r^2\).
Find the radius from the area at this instant, after differentiating.

steps.explain: Differentiate with respect to time; r depends on time.
Find r at the instant A=0.3.
Solve for the radius rate and keep units.

questions.stem: The curve \(y=16-(x+1)^2\) is rotated about the x-axis. Which definite integral gives the volume of the resulting solid?
questions.hint: For rotation about the x-axis, use disks with radius y; find the x-intercepts for the bounds.

keyPoints.note: A cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a disk of radius y.
Set y=0 to find where the region meets the x-axis.

steps.explain: Find the x-intercepts to determine the limits of integration.
Rotating a vertical slice around the x-axis forms a disk of radius \(r=y\), with area \(\pi r^2\).
Integrate the disk areas between the two intercepts.

questions.stem: The shaded region bounded by \(xy=64\), \(x=4\), \(y=26\), and the coordinate axes is rotated about the y-axis. What is the flask capacity to the nearest millilitre?
questions.hint: Use horizontal disks: the radius is 4 cm until the curve meets x=4, then it is (64/y). Find the meeting height first.

keyPoints.note: Use horizontal slices and disk areas (\pi r^2).
Their intersection determines where the radius changes formula.

steps.explain: Find where \(xy=64\) meets \(x=4\): \(4y=64\), so the transition height is 16 cm. From y=0 to 16, the radius is 4.

steps.explain: From y=16 to 26, the boundary is the curve \(x=64/y\), so this is the disk radius.
Add the volumes of the two disk sections.
Evaluate and convert cubic centimetres to millilitres.

questions.stem: The area bounded by the line \(y=x-1\) and the curve \(y=4(x-1)^2\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis.

parts.stem: Sketch the bounded area, noting any intercepts.

steps.explain: Intercepts: the parabola touches the \(x\)-axis at its vertex \((1,0)\) and meets the \(y\)-axis at 4. The line meets the axes at \((1,0)\) and \((0,-1)\).
Shade between them; on \(1\lt x\lt\frac54\) the line is above the parabola (e.g. at \(x=1.1\): \(0.1\gt 0.04\)).

parts.answer: The parabola \(y=4(x-1)^2\) has vertex (1, 0) and y-intercept 4. The line \(y=x-1\) has intercepts (1, 0) and (0, −1). They meet where \(x-1=4(x-1)^2\), i.e. \(x=1\) or \(x=\frac54\), at (1, 0) and \(\left(\frac54,\frac14\right)\). The bounded area lies between them for \(1\le x\le\frac54\), with the line above the parabola.

keyPoints.note: The two graphs meet at x = 1 and x = 5/4 — factor (x − 1) out.

parts.hint: V = π∫(outer² − inner²) dx with outer = x − 1, inner = 4(x − 1)².

steps.explain: Rotating the region gives a solid with a hole: outer radius = the line, inner radius = the parabola, from \(x=1\) to \(x=\frac54\).
\(\frac{\pi}{192}\) is only the outer solid. Note: you must square each radius separately — not square the difference.

keyPoints.note: Washer method: π∫[(x − 1)² − (4(x − 1)²)²] dx from 1 to 5/4.
Replace sin²x by ½(1 − cos 2x) before integrating.

parts.stem: The graph of \(y=1+\sin x\) for \(0\le x\le\frac{3\pi}{2}\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid generated.
parts.hint: V = π∫(1 + sin x)² dx; expand and use part (i) for the sin²x part.

keyPoints.note: V = π∫y² dx. Expand (1 + sin x)² and reuse (i).

parts.answer: Chain rule: \(\frac{d}{dx}e^{u}=u'e^u\) with u = 2 sin x, u′ = 2 cos x.

parts.stem:
The region bounded by the graph \(y=\sqrt{\cos x}\,e^{\sin x}\) and the \(x\)-axis between \(x=0\) and \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis to form a solid.

Using the result from part i), find the exact volume of this solid.
parts.hint: V = π∫y² dx; y² = cos x e^(2sin x) — then use (i).

steps.explain: \(V=\pi\int y^2\,dx\), and squaring removes the square root.
Match part (i): multiply and divide by 2.

keyPoints.text: Using the result from part i)
keyPoints.note: Square y, then the integrand is half of the derivative in (i).

questions.stem:
In the diagram below, the region bounded by the curve \(y=2^x-2\) and the x axis between \(x=-1\) and \(x=2\) is rotated through one revolution about the x axis.

Find in simplest exact form the volume of the solid formed.

steps.explain: Volume about the \(x\)-axis. (Squaring makes the part below the axis count positively.)
Evaluate each part between the limits.

keyPoints.text: is rotated through one revolution about the x axis
keyPoints.note: V = π∫y² dx from −1 to 2; squaring takes care of the part below the axis.
